definition: Aerial perspective is a secondary monocular cue used in judging visual depth or distance. It refers to perceiving the third dimension from atmospheric-looking changes in how things appear, as one of several less reliable one-eyed signs of depth.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Depth or Distance, Visual (perception of); pinned source text
